strings.text: The deposit, 2026–27

A **$2,500** non-refundable deposit, with a signed agreement, secures a place for an accepted student. It is credited toward the total tuition cost — so it is a timing obligation rather than an addition to the published rate, and it is the first instalment, not an extra cost.

strings.text: Providence Day partners with **Clarity** to assess need · **$65** application fee, paid by the family (2026–27). The school describes the application as taking under an hour and mobile-friendly, and runs family webinars at which Clarity walks through the application and the tax-verification process. Need is assessed on gross income, assets, liabilities, family size, and the number of children in tuition-based schools; assistance does not exceed demonstrated need and depends on the availability of school funds.
strings.t: Providence Day fè patenarya ak **Clarity** pou evalye bezwen · frè aplikasyon **$65**, fanmi an peye l (2026–27). Lekòl la dekri aplikasyon an kòm yon bagay ki pran mwens pase yon èdtan epi ki fasil sou telefòn, epi li fè webinè pou fanmi kote Clarity esplike aplikasyon an ak pwosesis verifikasyon taks la. Yo evalye bezwen an sou revni brit, byen, dèt, gwosè fanmi, ak kantite timoun nan lekòl ki gen frè eskolè; asistans lan pa depase bezwen ki demontre epi li depann de disponiblite fon lekòl la.

strings.text: A 1040 return, W-2s and the most recent pay stub — tax documents transfer automatically from the I.R.S. once verification is complete — plus business returns and 1099s for the self-employed. Documents are required from **both custodial and non-custodial parents**, whether divorced, separated or never married; the school states that missing information from either parent may affect eligibility.
strings.t: Yon deklarasyon 1040, W-2 ak dènye souch chèk la — dokiman taks yo transfere otomatikman soti nan I.R.S. la yon fwa verifikasyon an fini — plis deklarasyon biznis ak 1099 pou moun k ap travay pou tèt yo. Dokiman obligatwa nan men **tou de paran ki gen gad la ak sa ki pa gen gad la**, kit yo divòse, separe oswa yo pa t janm marye; lekòl la deklare enfòmasyon ki manke nan men nenpòt nan paran yo ka afekte kalifikasyon.

strings.text: The school states plainly that applying for assistance does **not** influence a candidate's admission selection, and that separate committees decide admission and assistance. It does not use the terms "need-blind" or "need-aware," so this report applies neither label.
strings.t: Lekòl la deklare klèman ke aplike pou asistans **pa** enfliyanse seleksyon yon kandida nan admisyon, epi ke komite apa deside admisyon ak asistans. Li pa sèvi ak tèm “need-blind” oswa “need-aware”, kidonk rapò sa a pa aplike ni youn ni lòt etikèt.

strings.text: Where the detailed figures live

strings.text: The tuition page omits every aid figure but one; the numbers live in the annual **Report on Philanthropy**, "Enrollment at a Glance." Published editions: **2012–13** $3,105,191 awarded, avg $12,273, 16% of students · **2013–14** $3,013,928, avg $12,664 · **2017–18** $3,683,971, avg $13,695, 16%. No comparable figures were located after 2017–18. A parent reading only the tuition page would never encounter any of this — a placement finding, not a disclosure gap.
strings.t: Paj frè eskolè a kite chak chif èd deyò eksepte youn; chif yo ap viv nan **Report on Philanthropy** anyèl la, “Enrollment at a Glance.” Edisyon ki pibliye: **2012–13** $3,105,191 yo bay, mwayèn $12,273, 16% nan elèv yo · **2013–14** $3,013,928, mwayèn $12,664 · **2017–18** $3,683,971, mwayèn $13,695, 16%. Nou pa t jwenn okenn chif konparab apre 2017–18. Yon paran k ap li sèlman paj frè eskolè a pa t ap janm rankontre okenn nan sa yo — yon konklizyon sou plasman, se pa yon mank nan divilgasyon.

strings.text: AVERAGE IS NOT MEDIAN
strings.t: MWAYÈN SE PA MEDYÀN

strings.text: Every award figure the school publishes is an **average grant** — reproduced unchanged and never treated here as a typical award. Aid awards carry a long upper tail, so an average usually sits above what a typical recipient receives; no median is published in any edition located, so a family cannot tell how far above.
strings.t: Chak chif prim lekòl la pibliye se yon **sibvansyon mwayèn** — nou repwodui l san chanje epi nou pa janm trete l isit la kòm yon prim tipik. Prim èd yo gen yon long ke anwo, kidonk yon mwayèn abityèlman chita pi wo pase sa yon benefisyè tipik resevwa; pa gen okenn medyàn ki pibliye nan okenn edisyon nou jwenn, kidonk yon fanmi pa ka di konbyen pi wo.

strings.text: A UNIT CHANGE THAT BLOCKS COMPARISON
strings.t: YON CHANJMAN INITE KI BLOKE KONPAREZON

strings.text: The historical editions count **students** receiving aid (16%); the current page counts **families** receiving assistance (≈21%). Different units, different bases — the apparent 16% → 21% movement cannot be read as growth in reach. It may be an artefact of the unit change, entirely real, or a mixture. This report declines to reconcile them.
strings.t: Edisyon istorik yo konte **elèv** k ap resevwa èd (16%); paj aktyèl la konte **fanmi** k ap resevwa asistans (≈21%). Inite diferan, baz diferan — mouvman aparan 16% → 21% la pa ka li kòm yon kwasans nan pòte. Li ka yon rezilta chanjman inite a, konplètman reyèl, oswa yon melanj. Rapò sa a refize rekonsilye yo.

strings.text: An internal discrepancy, reported not resolved
strings.t: Yon kontradiksyon entèn, nou rapòte l men nou pa rezoud li

strings.text: The 2012–13 Report on Philanthropy states **$3,105,191** as total aid awarded on its enrollment page and **$3,092,165** as the financial-aid line in its expense breakdown a page later — a **$13,026** difference, both published by the school in the same document. Both are reproduced; the likeliest explanation is different accounting bases, but the school does not say so and inferring it would be a guess.
strings.t: Report on Philanthropy 2012–13 la deklare **$3,105,191** kòm total èd yo bay sou paj enskripsyon li a epi **$3,092,165** kòm liy èd finansye a nan dekoupaj depans li yon paj apre — yon diferans **$13,026**, lekòl la pibliye tou de nan menm dokiman an. Nou repwodui tou de; eksplikasyon ki pi pwobab la se baz kontablite diferan, men lekòl la pa di sa epi dedwi sa ta yon devinèt.

strings.text: HOW AID IS FUNDED
strings.t: KIJAN YO FINANSE ÈD LA

strings.text: Assistance draws on both operating funds and endowment income. 2017–18: financial aid and discounts were **9.7%** of expenses against a stated $40.6M budget, and 5% of Annual Fund gifts were designated to Student Financial Assistance. 2012–13: a $3,092,165 aid line within a $33,320,795 expense total — a 9.3% share (our arithmetic on the school's two figures). Schedule I and Schedule D of the Form 990, which would carry the K–12 assistance and endowment detail, could not be retrieved.
strings.t: Asistans lan pran nan tou de fon operasyon ak revni dotasyon. 2017–18: èd finansye ak rabè te **9.7%** nan depans yo kont yon bidjè deklare $40.6M, epi 5% nan don Annual Fund yo te deziyen pou Student Financial Assistance. 2012–13: yon liy èd $3,092,165 anndan yon total depans $33,320,795 — yon pòsyon 9.3% (kalkil nou sou de chif lekòl la). Schedule I ak Schedule D nan Form 990 la, ki ta pote detay asistans K–12 ak dotasyon an, nou pa t kapab rekipere yo.

strings.text: This is the structural feature no other school on this roster has: **price depends on parish participation, not on grade level or financial need**. A participating Catholic family pays **$15,041** where a community family pays **$21,562** for the same seat in the same classroom — a **$6,521 difference, roughly 30%**. strings.text: Carmel Christian is a ministry of Carmel Baptist Church and, as a church-affiliated organisation, is **not required to file Form 990** — ProPublica returns no filing for the school itself. strings.text: Gaston Day runs need-based **Financial Aid**, **Merit Scholarships** and the **NC Opportunity Scholarship** as separate routes. A family may be eligible for more than one, and the interaction between them is not published — which is worth asking about directly.
strings.t: Gaston Day fè mache **Financial Aid** baze sou bezwen, **Merit Scholarships** ak **NC Opportunity Scholarship** kòm wout apa. Yon fanmi ka kalifye pou plis pase youn, epi entèraksyon ant yo pa pibliye — sa vo lapèn mande sou li dirèkteman.

strings.t: Barèm frè a deklare ke “Gaston Day offers a variety of payment plans in an effort to make our community more affordable and accessible” — men li pa nonmen okenn nan yo, li pa bay kantite vèsman, dat oswa frè.

strings.text: All payment plans "assume tuition deposit and fees have been paid" — so the deposit and the full fees column come first, whatever plan a family picks. The deposit amount is not published.
strings.t: Tout plan pèman yo “assume tuition deposit and fees have been paid” — kidonk depo a ak tout kolòn frè anplis la vini anvan, kèlkeswa plan yon fanmi chwazi. Montan depo a pa pibliye.

strings.text: This is the thinnest section of Gaston Day’s public record. No plan names, no installment schedule, no plan fees, no card-processing surcharge, no deposit amount, no late-payment policy, no withdrawal or refund terms, and no tuition-insurance or refund-plan offering appear anywhere on the public site. Every peer school here publishes at least the installment count.
strings.t: Sa a se seksyon ki pi mens nan dosye piblik Gaston Day a. Pa gen non plan, pa gen kalandriye vèsman, pa gen frè plan, pa gen sichaj pou trete kat, pa gen montan depo, pa gen politik pèman an reta, pa gen kondisyon pou retire oswa ranbousman, epi pa gen okenn asirans frè eskolè oswa plan ranbousman ki parèt okenn kote sou sit piblik la. Chak lekòl parèy isit la pibliye omwen kantite vèsman an.
